Subject: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth

Dear Requester,

Thank you for your emails dated 29 October 2026 regarding Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.

We have considered the information contained within your email and the additional search terms you have provided.

The Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR) provide a right of access to recorded environmental information held by a public authority. Regulation 2(1) defines environmental information and includes information concerning matters such as the state of the environment, factors affecting the environment, and measures or activities affecting or likely to affect the environment.

Having considered your correspondence, we do not consider that the information you have requested regarding the disconnection, shut off, cap, termination or otherwise interference with the water supply to Great House Farm constitutes a request for environmental information falling within the definition at Regulation 2(1) of the EIR.

The information requested relates to the disconnection of a specific property. The fact that information concerns a water supply to a property does not, of itself, make it “environmental information” for the purposes of regulation 2(1) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. The information must fall within one or more of the categories in regulation 2(1). The requested information concerns the fact and circumstances of the property's disconnection. It does not describe the state of any element of the environment, such as water, air, soil or land, within regulation 2(1)(a), nor does it concern a factor such as a substance, energy, noise, radiation, waste, emission, discharge or other release which affects or is likely to affect those elements within regulation 2(1)(b). Further, the disconnection is not a measure or activity affecting or likely to affect environmental elements or factors, or as one designed to protect them, within regulation 2(1)(c). The remaining limbs of regulation 2(1), concerning reports on environmental legislation, relevant economic analyses, and human health and safety or built structures insofar as they are affected by environmental elements, factors, measures or activities, are likewise not engaged.

As the request is directed to the disconnection of this property rather than to any environmental state, effect, factor, measure or activity within regulation 2(1), the information does not fall within the definition of environmental information under the EIR.

Even if this information were considered to be environmental information for the purposes of the Regulations, DCWW would have to refuse the request under Regulation 12(4)(a) as we do not hold the information requested. We do not hold the historical information sought. In accordance with our Retention Policy, any customer or property records from the 1980s that may have existed from that period would fall outside of our data retention periods., and we would no longer hold records dating back to that time. We are also unaware of any other public authority that may hold this information.

For this reason, we are unable to carry out the additional historical searches requested or provide an audit trail identifying search terms and systems in respect of information that is no longer held.

Your email also requested confirmation as to whether any surviving historic records, indexes, work-order records or archived material relating to Great House Farm/Ty Mawr exist. Some such information could constitute environmental information, depending on the nature of the information held and whether it fell within the definition of environmental information in Regulation 2(1). However, for the reasons set out above, we do not hold any historic records, indexes, work-order records or archived material falling within the scope of your request. We are therefore unable to determine whether any such information, if it existed, would constitute environmental information. In any event, as we do not hold the requested information, the request would fall to be refused under Regulation 12(4)(a). We are also unaware of any other public authority that may hold this information.

We hope this clarifies our position.

Thank you
Sumerah
Customer Care Team Leader
__________________________
Dŵr Cymru Retail Services

Dear Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water Information Governance Team,

Further search terms for my EIR request of 7 June 2026 concerning water-supply records for Great House Farm, Llandough

New information has come to light about historical and locality wording, including “Llandough Home Farm” in the checked 1881 census image. Please rerun or extend the relevant searches for my 7 June request using the following forms where applicable. Its original subject and period remain unchanged.

The site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr beside St Dochdwy’s Church at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Penarth and Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan. The primary location controls are Heneb/GGAT HER GGAT02038s, RCAHMW NPRN 20182 and grid reference ST16707335; the later development address is Church View Close, █████.

Farm and building forms: “Great House Farm”; “Great House Farm, Llandough”; “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”; “Great House”; “Great house”; “Greathouse”; “Tŷ Mawr”; “Ty Mawr”; “Ty-mawr”; “Ty Mawr Farm”; “Ty Mawr (Great House)”; “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Cydfin Farm”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; “Cedfin”; “Cydwin”; “Cedwyn”; “Cedfyn”; “Cefin”; “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm”; “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”; “Llandough Church Farm”; “Church Farm”; “former Great House Farm”; “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church”; “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”; and the descriptive forms “an 800-year-old house”, “the ten-roomed house”, “ancient Welsh house” and “the farm / the whole of the farm”.

Wider-estate forms: “Cedwyn Estate”, “Cydwin”, “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” and “Cwm Cydfin Wood”. “Cedwyn Estate” is the family’s working name, not a period name established by the records. The Bute catalogue’s █████ - 1824 range is not a specific date for its Ty Mawr wording; the 1824 Stewart survey records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, and “Cwm Cydfin Wood” appears in a 1902 Bute sale catalogue. These are search leads, not proof of the same holding or title.

Locality forms: “Llandough-juxta-Penarth”; “Llandough near Penarth”; “Llandough near Cardiff”; “Llandough, Penarth”; “Llandough, Cardiff”; “Llandough”; “Landoche-juxta-Cardif”; “Llandough / Leckwith”; “Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Urban District of Penarth”; “Llandochau”; “CF64”; and “Church View Close, █████”. “Landoche-juxta-Cardif” is a historical manor locator, not proof that every holding in a record with that locator is this site. “Llandough / Leckwith” is neighbouring parish and manorial context, not another farm name.

The 1881 census image reads “Llandough Home Farm”; I identify that address with this site, supported by directory references to John Williams at “Great house” / “Greathouse”. “Land Doc Home Farm” is a reported competing transcription. “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm” is a reported lead that does not appear on the checked census page. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are reported research leads whose underlying documents have not been checked; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are retained as search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Church Farm” and “Llandough Church Farm” are source-specific terms whose identity with this property is unresolved. “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)” is used on a 1994 development plan; the separate Rees-family Llandough Farm opposite the hospital must not be merged with this property solely on the name. Llandough near Cowbridge / Llandough Castle is a different place and outside scope.

records.transcript:
Dear Requester,



Many thanks for contacting WTSWW with this interesting enquiry, although I am afraid we are not in a great position to help.



We don't currently have any data relating to this site in the office - we may have had some historically but some of the relevant paperwork was lost in a fire in about 2003.



If we did have any data remaining after that, I gather it would most likely have been in reports by Mary Gillham, in which case it would have been passed to SEWBReC, who digitised her archive.



We can't be sure that there is anything relevant in there, but it's definitely worth looking into - perhaps get in touch with them to enquire if you haven't already? https://www.sewbrec.org.uk/



Many thanks and best of luck with your search,

█████

I am researching the history of Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and of the farmland and woodland between Llandough and Leckwith, Vale of Glamorgan.



The Trust's own history records that its Glamorgan predecessor began as the Glamorgan County Naturalists' Trust, founded in January 1961, later the Glamorgan Wildlife Trust, and that the present Trust was formed by merger in 2002. Please could you tell me:



(a) whether the Trust holds, or knows the present location of, any site files, survey records, maps or photographs for Llandough-juxta-Penarth or Leckwith (including the wooded slopes between the two) dating from about 1961 to 2002;

(b) whether any of those records mention Great House Farm, or record who was consulted as owner or occupier of the land; and

(c) if the older Glamorgan records have been deposited with an archive, which archive holds them and under what reference.



I would welcome a short acknowledgement.



Kind regards,



Requester

James
